data.name: Bacon Man: An Adventure
data.detailed_description:
Edição Deluxe digital

Download the Digital Deluxe Edition of Bacon Man and receive:
A copy of Bacon Man: An Adventure
The Bacon Man original soundtrack
PDF digital art book
Desktop wallpaper pack


Acerca do jogo

Story

Take on the role of Bacon Man and battle through the food groups to confront those who’ve condemned you. It’s up to you to clear his name and reclaim his rightful place on the Meat Throne.

Features


Tougher than nails platforming - in air, or on foot - using the patented "Bacon Control System™".

2 Player Couch Co-Op: Crush 25 levels with a friend. Choose from 4 unique characters, each with their own set of moves.

Obliterate enemies with versatile fighting moves like the Sky Divider, Dash, Stinger, Ground Pound... Each doubling as a method of mobility!

Collect experience, level up, and gain incredible new abilities through the power of tutorials! Unlock classy costumes for a sassy new look.

Play through a huge and satire-rich story…

...or straight up ignore the developers’ hard work by pressing the skip button.

Deep choices. Conversations.

reviews.review:
[h1]Bacon Man: An Adventure[/h1]

Another successful Kickstarter with another eager wait during the development process, [i]Bacon Man[/i] generated a good amount of hype with its outlandish premise and titular main character, off-the-wall visuals, and late 90's inspired platforming action. With an initial release date in December of last year, the game has received a bit of a pushback in order to polish up the experience and fans have been more than eager to get a taste of the pork-based adventure in full. It turns out it's been worth the wait, as the game ended up as entertaining, charming, and polished as you could want it.

[i]Bacon Man[/i] is easily one of the stranger if not more unique video game platformer heroes to appear since probably [i]Earthworm Jim[/i]. An anthropomorphic... strip of bacon? Or maybe he's like Earthworm Jim and is just a strip of bacon in a humanoid suit. Either way, he's pretty weird. He has a lot of friends that seem to be pigs, and they don't seem to really mind that he's them except cooked which is kinda weird too but they seem to like each other anyway. His other friends include some kind of feta cheese samurai, a freaky grizzled and feral ninja girl of some kind, and a really overweight Samurai Pizza Cat lady that looks like she ate a bit too much pizza named Lard Lass. You'll even befriend a boar dude named Excaliboar who for some reason isn't entirely down with your pork chomping antics, the heathen. The whole thing shows an incredible deal of imagination in its different eccentric and impressive environments of which there are seven, each with a selection of various well-designed and eye-opening levels of alternating paths, secret treasures and difficult bosses just as any 90's kid would remember them.

[h1]Visuals/Audio[/h1]

Right off the bat [i]Bacon Man[/i] has a very 90's Saturday Morning Cartoon feel about it, from the catchy title-screen and the appearance of the zany food-oriented cast of characters. It also has a very cheeky "anime" feel to it with the subtitle of the game being in katakana, and the opening song having little bits of what sounds like the plucking of Koto giving the game a strangely "Far-Eastern" feel to it. From the busty "Melon Maiden" who loads up your save files and greets you at the pub to the demonic meat creature that seems to be the boss dubbed simply the Pork King the character designs are funny and clever, and sure maybe a little grotesque and bizarre.

As you get into the adventure the tone of the soundtrack becomes more serious, orchestral, and adventurous while the visuals on enemies and setpieces remain as out-there as usual. Backgrounds consistently grow in quality and detail as you progress through the game, and are genuinely stunning pieces of eye-candy as far as sidescrollers go. Through icy frozen mountains with vibrant caves of pulsating organics and geysers in the background spewing clouds of flowing purple smoke, to the molten red volcanoes of trecherous and unpassable terrain it's all done in an incredibly vibrant and modern yet somehow cartoon-y and nostalgic way. 

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

You start out learning to combo, uppercut, and downward smash enemies with your fists and soon enough earn access to the trusty toaster gun with its slowly recharging shots. The bodies of knocked out enemies can be flung into each other for damage, or thrown onto water and turned into traversable blocks. Combat is telegraphed well into actual exploration and enemies can be uppercutted and comboed across gaps or smashed from above for a little bit of extra air. The combat becomes hectic and satisfying within only a couple levels, with enemies attacking you from both sides both close and long ranged forcing you to time your shields, conserve your ammo, and strike with the right rhythm to not get hit. It takes some practice to not get pummeled, but once you've got it down and the combos are flying with the bullets it feels good. Really good.

Each level has multiple directions you can venture out into and the less conventional seeming path will always be the harder one. Heavy but creative platforming sections make up a good deal of most of these paths, interspersed with plenty of enemies coming in from every direction to block, punch, and shoot. No matter what your path, levels generally end in a tough and chaotic and usually pretty damn fun boss fight of which many being reminiscent of the legendary [i]Mega Man[/i] bosses. There are four different bizarre and mostly food-related characters to choose from with unique traits and abilities. They all vary in speed, health, power meter and can of course each have their own individual experience and character level, which adds a lot of replay value and incentive to go back with new characters you want to strengthen. As if any extra incentive is needed to go back, with such eye-catching and vibrant stages and the many paths they hold. Each 'Ascension' grants you a choice of powering up your health or your power, and finding the important Wards strewn about levels or from enemies and bosses will be what grant you new skills and passives.

While a mostly fun and accessible yet brutal platforming romp, the game can be quite challenging in true retro tradition. With lots of high-health bosses that will test your reflexes and attacks that will require perfect timing of the shielding mechanic, and plenty of pixel-perfect jumping sections that will insta-kill you on failure this is still a difficult if not overall enjoyable sidescroller that will push you in the same way the classics of the 90's did. The actual platforming can be a tad frustrating due to a bit of floatiness while controlling Bacon Man in the air, which could be a side-effect of having to use the analog stick when I'm used to using a D-pad for platformers. Many times while trying to aim my landing on another jump pad to traverse the rows of jump pads leading to the next ledge I would miss my target by just a hair, and no matter how precisely I aimed Bacon Man would often inch just enough to one side to overshoot the target. Admittedly this is true of the 90's platforming classics this seems to be a nod towards, and if you're here for the nostalgic value everything you remember is here for better or for worse.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

[i]Bacon Man[/i] just might be that perfect alternative for those who were hyped for [i]Cuphead[/i]'s cartoonish and visually impressive take on the speed-running platformer genre, but were turned away by the oppressive difficulty. It has actually long and satisfying platforming and beat'emup sections with just as impressive massive and tricky bosses, with just as animated and memorable a style to it while creating a whole comedic vibe of its own. It even has local co-op for those couch gaming sessions with a friend. It's an oddly gorgeous game with some wacky as hell creative food-based setpieces and backgrounds, it's entirely accessible and easy to play on the surface while offering plenty of techniques to master and secrets to sidetrack yourself with for the more old school players. 

Visually you can see some serious heart and soul has been poured into the different stage and humorous character designs as well as how consistently each new stage blows you away in its massive, detailed, and polished appearance. For the stellar production quality alone, [i]Bacon Man: An Adventure[/i] is more than worth the asking price.
